subject: Activation cadence + evaluation gates — BankWell MAP & canary plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@bankwell.com>
Cc: Emma Lowe <emma.lowe@bankwell.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Activation cadence + evaluation gates — BankWell MAP & canary plan

Hi Sanjay / Emma,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — great alignment on objectives. Attached is our first draft MAP (MAP_BankWell_v1.xlsx) with an embedded post-signature implementation section covering: rollout phases, canary cohort approach, migration windows, and the training cadence for end-users and admins. I also attached a short evaluation plan (EvalPlan_BankWell.docx) that maps acceptance gates to automated checks and human sign-offs.

High-level proposal (week numbers counted from signature day = week 0):
- Week 0–1: Contract sign, SOW execution, procurement handoff (procurement@bankwell.com).
- Week 2: Provision dedicated environment and network peering; preflight security runbook.
- Week 3–4: Canary phase A (5% traffic, 3 internal teams + 1 pilot retail branch). Automated evals run each night; daily ops sync.
- Week 5: Canary phase B (25% traffic); stress and load evals, training for 2 ops teams.
- Week 6–7: Gradual migration (50% → 100%) with rollback windows and cutover scripts.
- Week 8: Knowledge transfer, final acceptance and runbook handoff.

Key asks from you today: confirm the target pilot branch set and whether procurement needs any specific SOW language beyond the standard template (we can provide DocuSign link). If the high-level weeks look good, we’ll finalize the MAP and circulate the canary runbook for technical sign-off.

We expect to include two gating checks during canary:
1) nightly accuracy regression on the agreed prompt set (EvalPlan includes the prompt list), and
2) p95 latency and error-rate thresholds (both in the MAP). If either gate fails, automatic rollback to the previous model variant is configured.

Attachments: MAP_BankWell_v1.xlsx (MAP with embedded post-signature tab), EvalPlan_BankWell.docx

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

---

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@bankwell.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emma Lowe <emma.lowe@bankwell.com>, procurement@bankwell.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation cadence + evaluation gates — BankWell MAP & canary plan

Vanessa —

Thanks for the draft. Overall this aligns with what our ops and retail pilots expect. A couple of adjustments we need before we commit:

1) Canary timing: would prefer Canary phase A to start week 4 instead of week 3 to allow our infra team extra time for network peering and compliance scans.
2) Pilot scope: we’ll start with 2 pilot branches (Downtown & Northside) and the Digital Customer Support queue, not the 3 internal teams.
3) Training: can the training be condensed into two 90-minute sessions per ops team (one admin + one end-user) so we can keep people billable?
4) Security questionnaire: we need the completed security/compliance questionnaire (SOC2 scope + data retention section) returned by 2028-06-27 for our infosec review.
5) SOW: Procurement expects SOW by 2028-06-28; they prefer a single-signed DocuSign SOW (we’ll countersign).

If you can update the MAP with those changes and send the security questionnaire, we’ll confirm.

Best,
Sanjay Patel
Senior PM, Platform Integrations | BankWell
sanjay.patel@bankwell.com

Subject: RE: FW: Activation cadence + evaluation gates — BankWell MAP & canary plan (runbook + cutover)

Vanessa / Jonas —

I can have the canary runbook and cutover artifacts ready by Monday 2028-06-25 EOD. Key technical plan (short):
- Canary sizing: Phase A = 5% traffic (~120 reqs/min), Phase B = 25% (~600 reqs/min). Pilot cohort = 2 retail branches + 1 digital queue.
- Model variants: start on v1.3-quant (lower memory); fallback to v1.2 if nightly accuracy drops >1.5% on the benchmark prompt set.
- KV cache warm-up: pre-warm via synthetic prefix traffic 2 hours before go-live; expect steady-state p95 latency ~110ms for warm runs, cold-warm delta ~45ms.
- Monitoring: daily automated accuracy job (EvalPlan) with Slack alert to #bankwell-ops and PagerDuty escalation on error-rate >0.5% across 1h window.
- Cutover script: Cutover_Script.sh (stub) performs traffic shift in 5% steps with 20m stabilization windows; includes health checks and auto-rollback trigger.

Training notes: I’ll provide a short tech walk-through deck for the admin session and a one-page quick reference for agents. Jonas — please let me know preferred format (slide vs runbook).

Attachments I will add to the shared drive: BankWell_Canary_Runbook.md, Cutover_Script.sh (executable stub).

Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
